function.name: add_component
function.description: Place one component. type: a type from list_component_types (AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NOR, XNOR, BUF, IN, OUT, VCC, GND, CONST, MUX, DFF, JKFF, TFF, SRFF, …) or 'block:<sheet name>' for a sub-circuit. Without x/y it goes to a free spot right of the drawing. Returns the part with its pins.

function.name: connect
function.description: Wire an output pin to an input pin (fan-out is fine; an input takes one driver). Give from/to, or `connections` [[from,to],…] for several. The new wires are routed. One bit of a bus pin takes an index — 'a', 'y.i[2]' or 's.o[3]', 'z' — and the bus tap is placed for you.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

from.description: Pin reference 'component.pin' (e.g. 'U1.i0', 'ff0.q') or a bare component.

to.description: Pin reference 'component.pin' (e.g. 'U1.i0', 'ff0.q') or a bare component.

function.name: disconnect
function.description: Remove wiring: `pin` drops every wire on that pin; `from`+`to` removes one connection.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

pin.description: Pin reference 'component.pin' (e.g. 'U1.i0', 'ff0.q') or a bare component.

from.description: Pin reference 'component.pin' (e.g. 'U1.i0', 'ff0.q') or a bare component.

function.name: delete
function.description: Delete components (and their wires). A net a deleted part drove is removed with it (no leftover wiring still 'driving' its sinks); the inputs it fed come back as now_unconnected.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: update_component
function.description: Rename, change params, change a basic gate's type, move (x/y) or rotate a component.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

ref.description: Component: id, INPUT/OUTPUT name, or label.

function.name: apply
function.description: Run several edit steps as one transaction — if a step fails nothing changes (unless keep_going). Each step is {"op": "add_component"|"connect"|"disconnect"|"delete"|"update_component"|"set_pins", …that tool's args}. Step fields (* = required): add_component: type* (string), name (string), width (integer), params (object), x (number), y (number), rot (integer); connect: from (string), to (string), connections (array), net_name (string); disconnect: pin (string), from (string), to (string); delete: refs* (array); update_component: ref* (string), name (string), params (object), type (string), x (number), y (number), rot (integer); set_pins: map* (object). Steps run in order and each sees the ones before it (delete then connect to the freed pin works).

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: build_part
function.description: Build a standard circuit from the part library on a sheet — generated by code and CHECKED against a reference model before it is drawn (every row, or 300 vectors / a clock-by-clock run), so it is right by construction and marked verified. Prefer this over drawing gates or typing truth tables. Place it on other sheets as block:<sheet>.

kind.description: a kind from list_parts, e.g. full_adder, adder, mux, bcd_7seg, mod_counter, clock_divider; lab parts: bcd_valid, one_pulse, counter_digit, bcd_counter_multi, bcd2_compare, add3, bin2bcd, hex_7seg, seg7_mux4, addsub, alu_slice, alu, register_en, mux_bus, bcd_ascii; a whole lab: lab6_counter (lab 6, counter 00-yy on the EDGE board: every block wired, pins mapped)

n.description: size: bits / inputs / modulus / divisor, per kind

ops.description: alu: '4' = ADD SUB XOR SHL (lab 9), '8' = NOP ADD SUB XOR SHL AND OR MOV (lab 10)

async.description: register_en: clear without waiting for the clock

tick.description: lab6_counter: 50 MHz clocks per count (default 2500000 = 20 Hz)

sheet.description: sheet to build on (created, or an empty one filled)

replace.description: rebuild a sheet that already has parts (one undo brings it back)

name.description: entity name when no sheet is given

function.name: list_parts
function.description: The part library: standard circuits (adders, subtractors, comparator, mux/demux, decoder, encoder, BCD→7-seg, parity, majority, counters, clock divider, shift register, register, toggle, edge detector, debounce) with their parameters and ports. `query` filters.

function.name: build_fsm
function.description:
Build a state machine from its state diagram: binary encoding (reset state = 0), minimised next-state and output logic, D flip-flops — then run clock by clock against the diagram before it is handed over (verified). fsm as text: 'inputs: x
outputs: z
state S0: z=0
state S1: z=1
S0 -> S1 when x
S0 -> S0 else
S1 -> S0 when ~x
reset S0' (Mealy: 'S0 -> S1 when x / z=1'; conditions & | ^ ~ ( ) else) or an object {inputs, outputs, states:[{name,out}], transitions:[{from,to,when,out?}], reset}. Ports: clk, the inputs, the outputs, state bits (state_out:false drops them).

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

replace.description: rebuild a sheet that already has parts (one undo brings it back)

function.name: build_hierarchy
function.description: Build a whole top sheet from a block list in ONE call: the blocks (an existing sheet or a library part), the top inputs / outputs, and the connections by name — buses expand to bits (cnt.ones = ones0..ones3, sw[3:0], x[2]), 0 / 1 drive a pin low / high. Widths, directions and double drivers are checked before anything is drawn; pins named like a top port join it (auto: a block's clk ← INPUT clk, OUTPUT err ← the one block output err). Drawn, routed, declared buses become bus ports; one undo step; nothing is left behind on an error. Answers what is still unconnected. Use it instead of many connect calls for any design made of blocks.

sheet.description: the top sheet (made, an empty one filled; one with parts needs replace:true)
an existing sheet

part.description: a list_parts kind, drawn once and verified

auto.description: join same-named pins and ports (default true)

bus.description: declared buses as bus ports (default true)

pins.description: board pins for the top ports, e.g. {'btn':'pb:4','sw[0]':'sw:0'}

top.description: also make it the project's top sheet

function.name: derive_spec
function.description: Derive a sheet's acceptance test from the user's REQUEST by code — independent of any circuit: equations in it, a minterm list (f(a,b,c) = Σm(1,2,4,7)), 'output 1 when the n-bit input is prime / even / > k …', or a standard part it names (4-bit adder, BCD→7-seg, mod-6 counter → checked against that part's reference model). With `sheet` it is set as that sheet's spec (the sheet is made if missing); a circuit that passes it is right, unlike a check against the table the circuit was built from. Answers derived:false when the request gives nothing to read.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

apply.description: false = only return the spec (default: set it on `sheet`)

function.name: set_spec
function.description: Say what a sheet MUST do — its acceptance test, written from the requirement (never from the circuit): formula ("sum = a^b^cin; cout = …"), table ({out:"0110…"}, first input = MSB) or sequence ({expect:{q:[0,1,2,…]}, inputs:[{name:value} per clock], cycles}). The app re-checks it after every change (✓/✗ on the sheet) and a pass marks the sheet verified. Set it FIRST, then build until check_spec passes.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: check_spec
function.description: Run a sheet's acceptance test (or every sheet's with all_sheets) and get pass / the mismatches.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: compare_sheets
function.description: Are two circuits the same? Drive `sheet` and `with` (another sheet) with the same inputs, port by port by name, and compare every output: all rows up to 12 input bits (else corners + 1000 random vectors); with flip-flops, clock by clock from reset on the same random stimulus. Or compare `sheet` with a formula, a table (columns or ones), a library part (+ params) or the request's words — e.g. a student's gates against the reference. No AI involved.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: build_circuit
function.description:
Create a whole circuit, minimised and laid out by the editor, on a new sheet. One of:
• formula: equations — "sum = a ^ b ^ cin; cout = a&b | cin&(a^b)" or "{cout,sum} = a + b + cin" (& | ^ ~ ' and/or/xor/not; {…} on the left = arithmetic, MSB first). The truth table is computed for you — prefer this to typing columns.
• truth_table: {inputs:[...], ones:{out:[rows that are 1]}} — e.g. a 3-bit prime detector {inputs:['x2','x1','x0'], ones:{p:[2,3,5,7]}}; or {inputs:[...], outputs:[...], columns:{out:"0110…"}} (one char per row, 0/1/x, first input = MSB; into:"current" fills a sheet that has exactly those ports, e.g. a lab template)
• generator: {kind: mod_counter|jk_counter|sequence_counter|ripple_counter|shift_register|register|bcd_7seg, n, sequence, active_low} — jk_counter = synchronous JK-FF counter / clock divider like the lab's (clk_in → clk_out = MSB; output:'q' gives q0..qN; clk / output rename); clock_divider = divide clk_in by ANY n (2..2^31, e.g. 50 MHz → 20 Hz: n=2500000), one sheet, 50 % duty for even n
• intent: {module, components:[{id,type,name?}], nets:[{from:'id.pin', to:'id.pin'}]} — a sub-circuit is type 'block:<sheet name>', its pins are that sheet's port names and must be spelled ('cnt.en', 'cnt.q')

inputs.description: formula: input order (first = MSB); default: order of appearance

replace.description: rebuild a sheet that already has parts (one undo brings it back)

sheet.description: Sheet to build on: a new name creates that sheet, an existing EMPTY sheet is filled (one with parts is refused). Default: a new sheet named after `name`.

bus.description: Numbered ports become one bus port: true = every group (q0..q3 → q[3:0], yu0..yu3 → yu[3:0]), or a list of group names ['q']. Bit i = the number in the name; bus taps are drawn for you.

function.name: make_bus_ports
function.description: Turn numbered INPUT/OUTPUT ports of a sheet (q0..q3) into one bus port each (q, 4 bits) with bus taps, keeping the drawing. Only for a sheet no other sheet uses as a block yet (their wiring would come loose).

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: check
function.description: Design-rule check (what Vivado would reject + common mistakes): errors and warnings with the component and a suggested fix.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: simulate
function.description: Simulate a sheet — ports as numbers too (`table` / `values`: a bus or a numbered group q0..q3 is one value), and for flip-flops a text `waveform`. Combinational: full truth table (rows 'inputs → outputs', and per-output columns) up to 10 input bits; for more, or to check chosen rows, give `vectors` [{input: value, …}, …] (≤256, inputs left out are 0, bus values as in probe). Sequential: `cycles` clock pulses on every INPUT that drives a flip-flop clock, other inputs held at `inputs` (default 0), or `vectors` = the inputs during each clock ([{x:1},{x:1},{x:0},…]; the last one stays).

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: verify_truth_table
function.description: Compare a combinational sheet against what it MUST do: expected output columns ({out:"0110…"}, x = don't care) or a formula written from the requirement ("sum = a^b^cin; cout = …"). Returns pass, the mismatching rows, `recognized` (the standard circuit it is, if any) and `independent` — an expectation identical to what the sheet was built from proves nothing and does not count as verified.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: probe
function.description: Set inputs and read every net's value (combinational evaluation) — find where a signal goes wrong. A bus INPUT takes its whole value: 5, "0101" (binary as wide as the bus), "0b0101" or "0x5"; a bus OUTPUT comes back as {value, bin}. Comparators, encoders, decoders, (de)muxes, bus taps are all evaluated. inside:'u' (or a path 'u/v') gives the nets and ports INSIDE that block instead, with its inputs from the whole circuit.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

inside.description: a block on the sheet (label / name), or a path u/v

function.description: Likely reasons a simulation doesn't behave as expected (clock not reaching FFs, reset stuck, gated clock, floating pins, multi-driver, constant outputs, unused inputs, divider chains).

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.description: Board pins as the lab sheet wires them, by each port's role: lab 6 (SW7–4 = tens of yy, SW3–0 = ones, centre button = start/stop, LED0 = error), lab 7 (SW15–0 = mm.ss digits, start/stop, clear), lab 8 (SW15–0 = four BCD digits); a–g, dp, an, clk on any lab. Answers what it could not place (auto_pins guesses those).

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: board_check
function.description: Before building the .bit: what will go wrong on the real EDGE board — ports without a pin, two ports on one pin, an input on an LED, 7-seg segments written active-high for this common-anode display, no digit enabled (an), a clock from a bouncing push button, a counter on the raw 50 MHz clock. Default sheet: the one the ลงบอร์ด page builds. fix:true repairs what it can (a NOT before each active-high a–g OUTPUT, an OUTPUT an0 = 0 on digit 0, pins guessed for ports without one) — one undo step each; `fixable` lists them otherwise.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: board_troubleshoot
function.description: The real board does not do what the simulation did: give the symptom (load, darkx, map, segpol, segan, segmap, fast, stuck, bounce, btninv; none = list them) and get the causes checked on this design (pins, polarity, clock source, reset, stale .bit) plus what to try.

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

function.name: suggest_wires
function.description: Wiring hints for the unconnected pins of a sheet: blocks of one kind in a row chain carry-like pins (cout→cin, x_out→x_in), a block input named like a sheet INPUT takes it (clk, rst, en; a2 or bit 2 of bus a for the block labelled …2), a sheet OUTPUT named like a block output takes it. Each hint has a reason; apply:true wires them all (one undo step).

sheet.description: Sheet name or id. Default: the active sheet.

Use it to follow how the course does something (a lab's requirements, a design method, a board connection).
